title: Apache Calcite Query Planning and Relational Algebra Documentation

sources.notes: Official overview describing Calcite as a dynamic data-management framework that provides parser, validator, optimizer, models, adapters, and query federation without owning storage or execution.
Official relational-algebra documentation for query trees, RelBuilder, logical operators, planner rules, semantic-preserving transformations, cost models, statistics, and extensible planning.
Official CSV-adapter tutorial covering SchemaFactory, Schema, model JSON, views, Table, ScannableTable, FilterableTable, TranslatableTable, relational operators, and planner rules.

Official adapter and driver documentation covering Arrow, Cassandra, CSV, Druid, Elasticsearch, File, Geode, InnoDB, JDBC, MongoDB, OS, Pig, Redis, Spark, Splunk, Kafka, Avatica, and JDBC connection properties.
Official model-file documentation for JSON/YAML schemas, tables, functions, types, materializations, schema cache behavior, map schemas, custom schemas, and JDBC schemas.
Official SQL grammar and parser reference for statements, queries, joins, pivots, unpivots, pattern recognition, grouping, windows, operators, data types, and dialect behavior.
Official lattice documentation for star/snowflake schema modeling, many-to-one constraints, cube materialization lattice concepts, materialized-view recommendations, dimensions, and measures.
Official materialized-view documentation for exposing views to Calcite, view-based query rewriting, substitution, structural matching, join/aggregate/rollup/partial/union rewrites, and limitations.
Official streaming SQL documentation for Calcite's SQL and relational-algebra extensions for streams, STREAM queries, stream/table combinations, windows, grouping sets, sorting, and punctuation.
Official HOWTO page covering build/test flows, integration tests, adapter implementation, creating planner rules, tracing, generated classes, and release validation boundaries.
Official ecosystem page identifying Calcite use for SQL parsing, query optimization, streaming SQL, data virtualization, federation, materialized-view rewrite, and cost-based optimization.

Source repository, release tarballs, generated docs, examples, adapter code, tests, dependencies, and logos remain boundary-checked for provenance, license notices, checksums, and redistribution before caching.
